nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a configuration with left cells $L$ (nearest first), head cell $h$ and right cells $R$ (nearest first), let $q'$ be a state and let $s$ be an action code. Acting on $k$ with $q'$ and $s$ gives a configuration with state $q'$, as follows. For $s = 0$ (move left), its head cell is the first entry of $L$, or the blank $0$ if $L$ is empty, its left cells are $L$ without its first entry, and its right cells…
nodes.title: Acting on a configuration

nodes.summary: The tape symbol of a bit $b$ is $1$ if $b$ is false and $2$ if $b$ is true; the symbol $0$ is the blank.
nodes.title: Symbol of an input bit

nodes.summary: For a code $c$, a list of bits $x$ and $T \in \mathbb{N}$, the configuration of $c$ on $x$ after $T$ steps is obtained from the initial configuration on $x$ by applying $T$ times the step of $c$, where a step leaves a halted configuration unchanged. It is the configuration after $T$ steps, or the halting configuration if the machine halts earlier.
nodes.title: Clocked configuration of a code

nodes.summary: A configuration of the simulation consists of a state $q \in \mathbb{N}$, the list of the cells left of the head (nearest first), the symbol in the cell under the head, and the list of the cells right of the head (nearest first); states and symbols are natural numbers.
nodes.title: Explicit configurations

nodes.summary: A code is a transition table: a finite list of rows, row $q$ belonging to the state $q \in \mathbb{N}$, each a finite list of entries, entry $a$ of a row belonging to the symbol $a \in \mathbb{N}$. The entry in row $q$ and column $a$ is either empty, meaning that the machine halts, or a pair $(q', s)$ of natural numbers, meaning that the machine enters the state $q'$ and does the action coded by $s$: $0$ moves…
nodes.title: Codes for single-tape machines

nodes.summary: A natural number codes a statement of a single-tape Turing machine with symbols in $\mathbb{N}$: $0$ moves the head left, $1$ moves the head right, and $a + 2$ writes the symbol $a$.
nodes.title: Decoding an action

nodes.summary: For a single-tape Turing machine $M$ and an input word $l$, the evaluation of $M$ on $l$ is defined (that is, $M$ halts on $l$) if and only if there is $T \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $M$ halts on $l$ within $T$ steps.
nodes.title: Halting is halting within some number of steps

nodes.summary: For a code $c$ and a list of bits $x$, the machine decoded from $c$ halts on the input word of $x$ if and only if there is a clock $T \in \mathbb{N}$ for which the clocked evaluator of $c$ on $x$ with clock $T$ returns a result.
nodes.title: Unclocked halting

nodes.summary: Configurations correspond bijectively to tuples in $\mathbb{N} \times \mathrm{List}(\mathbb{N}) \times \mathbb{N} \times \mathrm{List}(\mathbb{N})$: a configuration corresponds to the tuple of its state, its cells left of the head, its cell under the head and its cells right of the head.
nodes.title: Configurations as tuples

nodes.summary: Codes for single-tape machines correspond bijectively to transition tables, that is, to lists of rows, each a list of entries that are either empty or a pair of natural numbers: a code corresponds to its table.
nodes.title: Single-tape codes as tables

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a code, $x$ a list of bits, $T$ a natural number and $l$ a list of natural numbers. If the clocked evaluator, running $c$ on $x$ for at most $T$ steps, returns $l$, then the decoded machine of $c$, started on the input word of $x$, halts, and the tape from its head rightwards in the halting configuration is $l$ followed by blanks.
nodes.title: Clocked results agree with the machine's semantics

nodes.summary: For a code $c$, a list of bits $x$, a clock $T \in \mathbb{N}$ and a list $l$ of natural numbers, the clocked evaluator returns $l$ on $c$, $x$ and $T$ if and only if the configuration of $c$ after $T$ clocked steps on $x$ has no successor step and its output is $l$.
nodes.title: Characterization of clocked results

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a code for a single-tape machine, $x$ a list of bits, $l$ a list of natural numbers and $T \le T'$ natural numbers. If the clocked evaluator returns $l$ on $c$ and $x$ with clock $T$, then it also returns $l$ with clock $T'$.
nodes.title: Monotonicity of the single-tape clocked evaluator

nodes.summary: Given a code $c$, a list of bits $x$ and a clock $T \in \mathbb{N}$, run the simulation of $c$ on $x$ for at most $T$ steps. If it halts within $T$ steps, the result is the output of the halting configuration: the tape from the head rightwards, with trailing blanks dropped. Otherwise there is no result.
nodes.title: The clocked evaluator

nodes.summary: Universality of codes, for machines that read bit inputs. Let $M$ be a single-tape Turing machine with a finite alphabet $\Gamma$ and a finite set of states that contains the initial state and is closed under the transitions of $M$, and let $\iota$ be an injective map from the bits to $\Gamma$ whose values are not the blank. Then there are a code $c$ and an injective map $f$ from $\Gamma$ to the natural numbers,…
nodes.title: Universality of codes

nodes.summary: For a code $c$, a list of bits $x$ and $T \in \mathbb{N}$, the decoded machine of $c$ halts within $T$ steps on the input word of $x$ if and only if the explicit simulation of $c$, started from the initial configuration on $x$, reaches after some $j \le T$ steps a configuration that has no successor step.
nodes.title: Bounded halting of a decoded machine through its simulation

nodes.summary: A single-tape Turing machine $M$ halts within $T$ steps on a word $l$ when, started in its initial state with $l$ on the tape and the head on the first letter of $l$ (on a blank if $l$ is empty), it reaches after some $j \le T$ steps a configuration that has no successor.
nodes.title: Bounded halting of a single-tape machine

nodes.summary: For a list of bits $x$, the initial configuration of the simulation on $x$, read as a configuration of a single-tape machine, is the initial configuration of a single-tape machine on the input word of $x$.
nodes.title: The explicit initial configuration is the machine's

nodes.summary: The initial configuration of the simulation on a list of bits $x$ has state $0$, an empty list of cells left of the head, the head on the first symbol of the input word of $x$ (the blank $0$ if $x$ is empty), and the remaining symbols of the input word, in order, right of the head.
nodes.title: Initial configuration of the code simulation

nodes.summary: The input word of a list of bits $x$ is the list of natural numbers obtained from $x$ by replacing each bit by its symbol: $1$ for false and $2$ for true.
nodes.title: Input word of a list of bits

nodes.summary: For a code $c$, a list of bits $x$ and a clock $T \in \mathbb{N}$, the clocked evaluator of $c$ on $x$ with clock $T$ returns a value if and only if the simulation of $c$ has no step from the configuration after $T$ clocked steps on $x$ (the configuration after $T$ steps, or the halting configuration if the machine halts earlier).
nodes.title: Definedness of the clocked evaluator

nodes.summary: For a code $c$, a list of bits $x$ and a clock $T \in \mathbb{N}$, the clocked evaluator of $c$ on $x$ with clock $T$ returns a value if and only if the machine of $c$, started on the input word of $x$, halts within $T$ steps.
nodes.title: Clocked halting

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a code, $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and $k$ an explicit configuration. Run the machine of $c$ for $n$ steps from the Mathlib configuration of $k$, and run the explicit simulation of $c$ for $n$ steps from $k$, where a run that reaches a configuration without a successor before completing $n$ steps has no result. Then the first run has a result exactly when the second does, and its result is the Mathlib…
nodes.title: Iterated steps of the decoded machine

nodes.summary: For a code $c$ and numbers $q$ and $a$, the lookup of $c$ at state $q$ and symbol $a$ is the entry in row $q$, column $a$ of the table of $c$: either a pair $(q', s)$ of a next state and an action code, or no entry (halt). It is no entry when the table has no row $q$ or that row has no column $a$.
nodes.title: Table lookup of a code

nodes.summary: The machine of a code $c$ is the single-tape Turing machine with states and symbols in $\mathbb{N}$ that, in state $q$ reading symbol $a$, halts if the table lookup of $c$ at state $q$ and symbol $a$ has no entry, and otherwise, if the entry is $(q', s)$, enters state $q'$ and does the action coded by $s$: $0$ moves left, $1$ moves right and $a' + 2$ writes $a'$.
nodes.title: The machine of a single-tape code

nodes.summary: For a single-tape Turing machine $M$, a list $l$ of symbols and numbers $T \le T'$, if $M$ started on $l$ halts within $T$ steps, then $M$ started on $l$ halts within $T'$ steps.
nodes.title: Halting within a bound is monotone in the bound

nodes.summary: The output of a configuration $k$ is the list consisting of the symbol under the head of $k$ followed by the cells right of the head (nearest first), with all trailing blanks $0$ removed.
nodes.title: Output of a configuration

nodes.summary: The clocked evaluator is primitive recursive in the code, the input and the clock.
nodes.title: The clocked evaluator is primitive recursive

nodes.summary: For every explicit configuration $k$, the half-tape of the Mathlib configuration of $k$ from the head rightwards (the cell under the head followed by the cells to its right) is the output of $k$, read with blanks beyond its end.
nodes.title: The output of a configuration as a Mathlib half-tape

nodes.summary: The set of states of a code $c$ is the finite set of natural numbers consisting of the initial state $0$ and every state $q'$ such that some entry of the table of $c$ is a pair $(q', s)$.
nodes.title: States of a single-tape code

nodes.summary: For a code $c$ and a configuration $k$ of the simulation, the configuration after one step of $c$ from $k$ if that step is defined, and $k$ itself if $c$ halts at $k$.
nodes.title: One step of a code, or stay when halted

nodes.summary: For every code $c$ and every configuration $k$ of the simulation, the decoded TM0 machine of $c$ halts at the TM0 configuration of $k$ exactly when the step of $c$ from $k$ is undefined, and otherwise its step from the TM0 configuration of $k$ is the TM0 configuration of the step of $c$ from $k$.
nodes.title: Explicit steps agree with the decoded machine

nodes.summary: For a code $c$ and a configuration $k$ of the simulation, look up the table entry of $c$ at the state of $k$ and the symbol under the head of $k$. If there is no entry, the step is undefined (the machine halts); if the entry is $(q', s)$, the step is the configuration obtained from $k$ by entering the state $q'$ and doing the action coded by $s$.
nodes.title: One step of a code

nodes.summary: The decoded machine is supported by the finite set of states of its code.
nodes.title: Codes denote finite machines

nodes.summary: The TM0 configuration of a configuration $k$ of the simulation has the state of $k$, the cell under the head of $k$ as its head cell, and as the halves of its tape left and right of the head the cells of $k$ left and right of the head, nearest first, followed by infinitely many blanks.
nodes.title: TM0 configuration of a simulation configuration

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
